text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
BURSA
- Romania's sole aluminium producer ALRO Slatina will be listed on the first tier of the Bucharest bourse.
ADEVARUL
- Romanian farmers will not be affected by the country's integration into the Central European Free Trade Association (CEFTA), a Trade Ministry official is quoted as saying.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The State Ownership Fund will put 2,565 companies in private hands this year, according to a draft programme presented to parliament.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The Renel RA electricity authority plans to set a 30 percent cut in electricity bills for industrial consumers which save energy and pay their bills in time.
- Romania will discuss with IMF plans to raise its foreign debt level and borrow an extra two billion dollars this year, Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea ias quoted as saying.
- Some analysts believe Romania's CEFTA membership will be a "disaster" for the country's farming sector, following cuts in import duties for food and farm products.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- President Emil Constantinescu and Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea still enjoy strong popular support, according to an opinion poll carried out by the Centre for Urban and Regional Sociology (CURS).
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- U.S. President Bill Clinton's visit to Romania next week shows support for the country's reforms and for the centrist cabinet, the paper says. It is also a "positive signal" sent to Romanians disappointed by the U.S.'s reluctancy to accept Romania in the first wave of a NATO enlargement this month, it said.
- More than 50 percent of Romanians trust Ciorbea's centrist government, but only 47 percent believe that reforms will be successful, the CURS opinion poll shows.
ADEVARUL
- Most politicians lost popularity in recent months, with ex-president Ion Iliescu losing 24 percentage points and Constantinescu six points, the CURS poll shows.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Parliament will meet in extraordinary session over July 1-10 to discuss vital reforms, including amendments to a 1991 land restitution law. ($ = 7,032 lei)
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
